answer: Reputation-weighted peer sampling. Each agent periodically samples neighbors and scores their responsiveness along a single thread of interaction history; scores propagate only one hop, so a node's standing reflects local reciprocity rather than self-asserted claims. New identities must be independently sampled and sustained by real peers before gaining weight, and the sampling vine spreads only through verified exchanges.
